rawFindings.title: Allow header may have duplicate HTTP methods for OPTIONS requests
rawFindings.explanation: The original code used appendMethods to add unique HTTP methods to the options array when processing an OPTIONS request. The patch replaces this with options.push.apply(options, route._options()), which directly appends methods without filtering duplicates. This can lead to duplicate method entries in the Allow header, which is incorrect behavior per HTTP specifications.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the use of appendMethods to ensure only unique methods are included in the options list, avoiding duplicates in the Allow header for OPTIONS responses.

rawFindings.title: Potential duplicate methods in OPTIONS header after abandoning duplicate check
rawFindings.explanation: The change replaces appendMethods(options, route._options()), which appended methods avoiding duplicates, with options.push.apply(options, route._options()), which blindly concatenates all methods from route._options() to options array, possibly introducing duplicate HTTP methods in the 'Allow' header for OPTIONS requests.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore duplicate checking when appending methods to options. For example, revert to using appendMethods or implement another deduplication method before sending the 'Allow' header.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect Allow header in OPTIONS response permits duplicate HTTP methods
rawFindings.explanation: The code change replaced a de-duplicating method (appendMethods) with a direct push of methods into the options array (options.push.apply(options, route._options())), which can lead to duplicate methods in the Allow header for OPTIONS requests.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the use of appendMethods to append HTTP methods to the options array, ensuring duplicates are not added. Replace line 210 with: appendMethods(options, route._options());
